etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Old French surmis, past participle of surmetre, surmettre (“to accuse”), from sur- (“upon”) + metre (“to put”).
senses: Thought, imagination, or conjecture, which may be based upon feeble or scanty evidence; suspicion; guess.
(intransitive) To imagine or suspect; to conjecture; to posit with contestable premises.
